2.4a — Prefabs, Spawning & Playtesting

You have a working coin, spike, and potion — singular. Games need dozens of each. Prefabs are the factory: build once, stamp many, change the master and every copy updates. Then, the professional ritual that runs the rest of your year: playtesting.

Build Lab ~25 min

Step 1 — read the blue bars. Drag three coins and two potions into the Overworld scene from Assets/Prefabs. In the Hierarchy each has a blue cube icon: that marks a prefab instance — a stamped copy of a master. Select one and the Inspector shows the master's fields plus overrides (the position).

Step 2 — change the master. Open the Coin prefab itself (double-click it, or Open Prefab). Change something visible — rotate its sprite, scale it 1.5×. Save and return to the scene: every coin in the scene updated. That is the whole deal — one edit, all copies. Now change one instance's scale in the scene: the Inspector shows the field in bold as an override. Master edits still propagate everywhere you did not override.

Deleting a prefab's master file while copies live in scenes = missing-script chaos. The prefab IS the object's definition; the scene stores "a copy of that file, at this position." Treat master files like production code.

Step 3 — Read the Spawning API. In games, many objects are not pre-placed in the scene by hand; they are stamped dynamically into existence at runtime. Unity provides the Instantiate() function to create instances of prefabs from code:

Function SignatureReturn TypeDescription & Behavior
Instantiate(original, position, rotation) Object (or GameObject) Clones the specified prefab asset or GameObject at the given 3D coordinates with the given orientation.
Quaternion.identity Quaternion Represents "no rotation" — the object aligns perfectly with the world coordinate axes.

Look at how a signaling flare launcher stamps instances of a prefab template into the world:

using UnityEngine;

// Launches distress flares from a prefab template
public class FlareLauncher : MonoBehaviour
{
    // Slot in Inspector to assign the master prefab asset
    [SerializeField] private GameObject flarePrefab;

    private void Update()
    {
        // When F is tapped, stamp a new clone into the world
        if (Input.GetKeyDown(KeyCode.F))
        {
            Instantiate(flarePrefab, transform.position, Quaternion.identity);
        }
    }
}
Architectural Challenge — Build a Dynamic Item Spawner:

Create your own testing script (e.g. ItemSpawner.cs) attached to an empty GameObject. Expose a [SerializeField] private GameObject itemPrefab; slot. Inside Update(), check for a key press (such as KeyCode.P) and call Instantiate() using your prefab slot, the spawner's transform.position, and Quaternion.identity. Assign your Coin or Potion prefab in the Inspector and test it in Play mode!

Bug Hunt: Factory faults

  1. Drag a plain coin sprite into the spawner slot instead of the prefab. What happens at spawn — and what IS the difference between an asset and a scene object?
  2. Spawn a potion instead. Does the tag still work? What does that prove about where identity lives?
  3. Delete the Coin prefab from Assets/Prefabs while three copies sit in the scene. What does Unity show you — and why is this the trap the callout warned about?
Playtest ~25 min

From today until June, this is the loop that makes every unit real: swap seats, play someone else's build, write what happened, fix the top three. Print the playtest sheet from Canvas (or copy its table into your journal):

ColumnWhat you write
What happenedFacts only: "died 4 times in the spike hall"
How it feltOne adjective per row: cheap, tense, confusing, satisfying
The fix I would tryOne concrete change: "move potion before the narrow hall"

The rules that make playtests honest: the tester plays and talks out loud but does not explain yet; the designer watches silently and takes notes; no defending, no arguing, no "you're holding it wrong." Then swap. Note that you will run this exact sheet on real data in 9.5a, where the whole class's sheets become a dataset you will analyze — you are generating a dataset right now. Every jam this year ends with this ritual; the AP exam calls evaluating and refining (CRD-2) the same skills you are practicing by swapping seats.

Tinker: Your build, under review

  1. Watch a partner play your Overworld for 3 minutes. Where did they hesitate, and what did they miss without being told?
  2. Pick your top-3 fixes and fix exactly one today. Why is fixing one at a time the discipline, not slowness? (Hint: what would you learn if you changed three things at once?)
  3. Commit + push: "2.4a: prefab factory + first playtest".

Checkpoint — before moving on, you must be able to:

  • Explain prefab master vs instance, and show an override in bold in the Inspector
  • Edit a master and see every instance update
  • Instantiate a prefab from code and explain why play-mode spawns vanish
  • Run a silent playtest and turn notes into exactly one fix
